title: Family Residence Permit in Türkiye: Spouses & Children Step-by-Step

quickAnswer: Türkiye's Family Residence Permit (Articles 34–37 of Law No. 6458) allows Turkish citizens, Blue Card holders, and qualifying foreign residence or work permit holders to sponsor their foreign spouse and minor or dependent children for up to three years at a time. Sponsors must meet income, housing, clean-record, and household health-insurance standards.

body.text: At [Itinerary of Türkiye](https://itineraryofturkiye.com/), our two founders organize flat-fee scouting trips, school-district orientation, and independent local introductions across Türkiye. We are paid by our clients and remain independent of provider commissions. Because residence permit filings, document legalization, and citizenship advice belong strictly to licensed Turkish attorneys and official bodies like the Presidency of Migration Management (Göç İdaresi) and Nüfus, use this overview to prepare before consulting legal counsel.
Who qualifies to sponsor a Family Residence Permit (Turkish citizen or work/Ikamet holder)?

Under Article 34 of Law No. 6458 and the [Presidency of Migration Management FAQ](https://en.goc.gov.tr/frequently-asked-questions-about-foreigners), eligible sponsors include Turkish citizens, Blue Card holders, foreigners holding a valid work permit or residence permit (generally after one year of residence in Türkiye), and refugees or subsidiary protection beneficiaries. Sponsors can cover one foreign spouse plus minor or dependent foreign children.

Foreign sponsors must typically have resided legally in Türkiye for at least one year before sponsoring family members, though exceptions exist for certain work permit and scientific-research categories. Under [Göç İdaresi Residence Permit Types](https://en.goc.gov.tr/residence-permit-types), a family permit lasts up to three years per issuance and can never exceed the sponsor's own permit duration. Children under 18 holding a family permit may attend primary and secondary schools without a separate student Ikamet.

body.text: What Apostilled marriage/birth certificates and income proofs are required?

Under Article 35 of Law No. 6458, sponsors must document monthly household income at least equal to the Turkish minimum wage and no less than one-third of the minimum wage per family member. Foreign marriage and birth certificates must carry a Hague Apostille (or consular legalization), sworn Turkish translation, and Turkish notarization.

In 2026, with Türkiye's net statutory minimum wage at TRY 28,075.50 (gross TRY 33,030), a family of four must demonstrate total monthly income above one-third of the minimum wage multiplied by four. Both spouses and children also submit clean criminal records where applicable—specifically proving the sponsor has no convictions for crimes against family order in the preceding five years. Prepare this checklist before filing on [e-Ikamet](https://e-ikamet.goc.gov.tr/):

items: Civil status records: Apostilled marriage certificate and children's birth certificates (plus notarized consent from any non-accompanying parent).
Income verification: Turkish payroll slips, tax filings, pension letters, or stamped bank statements confirming regular income.
Housing and address proof: Notarized lease or title deed (Tapu) showing accommodation meeting general health and safety standards.
Criminal record check: Sponsor's Turkish judicial record (and foreign record if residing in Türkiye under five years).
Application receipts: Printed [e-Residence required documents list](https://e-ikamet.goc.gov.tr/Ikamet/IstenenBelgeler) and paid fee receipts.

body.text: How does health insurance cover the whole household?

Turkish law requires active health insurance covering the sponsor and every sponsored family member for the full requested permit period. According to [Göç İdaresi General Information](https://en.goc.gov.tr/general-information41), acceptable proofs include an e-signed Social Security Institution (SGK) authorization certificate covering the whole family, bilateral social security agreement forms, a General Health Insurance (GSS) application receipt, or individual Turkish private health policies.

If the sponsor works in Türkiye with active SGK payroll contributions, adding a spouse and minor children as SGK dependents is often the cleanest route. When the sponsor is not covered by SGK, each adult family member needs a compliant Turkish private health policy matching the exact permit dates. Children under 18 and adults over 65 face different private-policy exemptions, so verify your household's exact requirement with your insurer and attorney before the appointment.
When can spouses apply for Turkish citizenship (3 years)?

Under Article 16 of Turkish Citizenship Law No. 5901, a foreign spouse married to a Turkish citizen does not receive citizenship automatically, but may apply after completing at least three continuous years of legally registered civil marriage. The couple must live together in family unity, avoid conduct incompatible with marriage, and pass national-security checks.

The three-year clock runs from the civil marriage date registered with Turkish authorities—or from the date the spouse acquired Turkish citizenship if naturalization happened after the wedding. Applications are filed at the Provincial Directorate of Population and Citizenship (İl Nüfus ve Vatandaşlık Müdürlüğü), followed by a local police home verification and a joint commission interview.

If your family is planning a scouting visit to compare cities, schools, and neighborhoods before relocating, read more [about Itinerary of Türkiye](https://itineraryofturkiye.com/about) and get in touch. Please never include passport or ID scans, medical or financial records, or payment details in your first enquiry.

faq.q: Can a tourist Ikamet holder sponsor a Family Residence Permit?
faq.a: Yes, if the sponsor has legally resided in Türkiye for at least one year, meets the Article 35 income and housing thresholds, and holds valid coverage for all family members.

faq.q: How long is a Turkish Family Residence Permit valid?
faq.a: Under [Göç İdaresi regulations](https://en.goc.gov.tr/residence-permit-types), a family permit is issued for up to three years at a time, and never beyond the sponsor's own permit expiration date.

faq.q: Do children on a Family Residence Permit need a separate Student Ikamet for school?
faq.a: No. Children under 18 holding a valid family residence permit have the right to attend primary and secondary schools in Türkiye without obtaining a student permit.

faq.q: What happens to a Family Residence Permit if the couple divorces?
faq.a: A foreign spouse married to a Turkish citizen who held a family permit for at least three years may apply to switch to a short-term residence permit; domestic-violence victims verified by court order are exempt from the three-year threshold.

faq.q: Does marriage to a Turkish citizen automatically grant Turkish citizenship?
faq.a: No. Spouses must wait three full years of registered civil marriage, maintain family unity, and complete a formal Nüfus application, investigation, and commission interview.

faq.a: No. [Itinerary of Türkiye](https://itineraryofturkiye.com/) coordinates scouting trips, orientation, and independent introductions; licensed Turkish attorneys and official authorities handle legal filings.
